items.locator: CDC STI Treatment Guidelines — Adolescents, Legal Issues and Confidentiality: all 50 states and DC explicitly allow minors to consent for their own STI services; age provisions for some services and confidentiality/notification rules vary by jurisdiction.
items.version: CDC STI Treatment Guidelines 2021 remain the live CDC guideline in 2026; page and legal caveats rechecked 2026-08-15. Current state law/policy must be applied at the point of care.

options.A: Federal law requires parental consent for all STI testing and treatment of minors, so care cannot begin until a parent authorizes it.
options.B: Minors can consent to STI services in every state and DC, but age, confidentiality, notification, and service-specific details can vary; apply current jurisdiction law and policy.
options.C: Minors can consent to STI testing nationwide but never to treatment, so a parent must authorize medication in every jurisdiction.
options.D: Only emancipated minors may independently consent to STI services; non-emancipated adolescents always require a parent to be present.

items.rationale: CDC states that every state and the District of Columbia explicitly allow minors to consent for their own STI services, while age provisions for some services and confidentiality or notification rules can vary. Therefore the nurse should recognize the general consent authority while applying current jurisdiction-specific law and policy and explaining confidentiality limits. The other options incorrectly impose universal parental-consent, testing-only, or emancipation requirements.

items.locator: 45 CFR §164.508(a)(2) / HHS HIPAA guidance on psychotherapy notes: authorization is generally required for use or disclosure of psychotherapy notes, subject to limited enumerated exceptions; psychotherapy notes receive protections beyond ordinary medical records.
items.version: Current HIPAA Privacy Rule and HHS guidance; medical-record guidance last reviewed 2025-05-30 and regulation currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.locator: ONC 2025 SAFER Guide — Computerized Provider Order Entry with Decision Support: recommended practices address design, implementation, testing, use, monitoring, and improvement of orders, alerts, warnings, and clinical decision-support safeguards.
items.version: 2025 SAFER CPOE with Decision Support guide; HealthIT.gov page updated 2026-04-28; rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.locator: AHRQ PSNet — Second Victims: Support for Clinicians Involved in Errors and Adverse Events: clinicians involved in errors/adverse events can experience substantial emotional and professional distress and may need structured peer/organizational support.
items.version: AHRQ PSNet primer reviewed in 2025; current federal patient-safety resource rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.rationale: The described guilt, anxiety, and loss of professional confidence after involvement in a serious error are consistent with the clinician-distress response commonly called the second-victim phenomenon. The concept describes the emotional and professional impact of an adverse event; it does not itself establish incompetence, and recovery may benefit from peer and organizational support.

items.locator: The Joint Commission — Sentinel Event FAQs: organizations should identify sentinel events, examine root causes and contributing factors, and make improvements/actions to mitigate risk of recurrence rather than focus the analysis on individual blame.
items.version: Current Joint Commission sentinel-event guidance in 2026; page and current expectations rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.locator: AHRQ — Defining the Patient-Centered Medical Home: five core attributes are comprehensive care, patient-centered care, coordinated care, accessible services, and quality and safety, typically supported by team-based primary care.
items.version: Current AHRQ PCMH definition at cited federal URL; rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.locator: CMS — Value-Based Programs: value-based programs reward health care providers with incentive payments for quality of care and move payment toward quality rather than quantity/service volume alone.
items.version: CMS Value-Based Programs page modified 2026-03-10; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.locator: AHA/ASA 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke — Emergency brain imaging/reperfusion evaluation: brain imaging is essential before acute reperfusion therapy to exclude intracranial hemorrhage; noncontrast CT rapidly detects acute hemorrhage.
items.version: AHA/ASA 2026 acute ischemic stroke guideline, current in 2026; currentness rechecked after the July 2026 guideline correction on 2026-08-15.

items.locator: American Stroke Association — Transient Ischemic Attack: transient stroke-like focal neurologic symptoms may resolve but still require emergency assessment because TIA signals near-term stroke risk; comprehensive evaluation is recommended urgently.
items.version: Current American Stroke Association TIA guidance; rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.locator: American Epilepsy Society evidence-based convulsive status epilepticus treatment algorithm — stabilization phase 0–5 minutes; initial therapy phase 5–20 minutes; benzodiazepines are recommended initial therapy for ongoing generalized convulsive seizure activity.
items.version: AES evidence-based convulsive-status guideline remains the listed foundational treatment guidance in 2026 while an updated status-epilepticus guideline is in development; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
